info.title: General
info.html:
Regular monsters have a monster level equal to the level of the zone they're found in and champion/unique monsters have a monster level that is +2/+3 higher than that. A monster's level determines which treasure classes it can drop items from. Monsters drop items with item levels equal to their monster level, which influences the affixes and sockets those items can get. Note that super unique monsters can have monster levels which don't follow this general format.

Changes

  • Many zones have had their zone level increased (shown below; included in-game next to the zone name in the upper right corner)
  • The 3 red portal zones in Act 5 (Abaddon, Pit of Acheron, Infernal Pit) have had their density increased by 40-50%, and Mausoleum & Crypt have had their density increased by 9%
  • The Maggot Lair and Arcane Sanctuary in Act 2 have wider pathways
  • Lower Kurast no longer has super chests due to their mismatched risk/reward

info.title: Level 85 Zone Info
info.html:
Level 85 zones are the zones in which the highest level items (TC 87) can be found from both champion and unique monsters since 85+2 and 85+3 are both at least 87. This means the highest level items can also be found in level 84 zones from unique monsters.

Many zone levels were increased to 85 so there are more endgame places to farm. Keep in mind that some zones are still worth farming even if they aren't level 85. Even if all items can't be found within lower level zones, they may have other advantages such as higher monster density, fewer immune/resistant monsters, more monster types that have better drop chances for valuable non-equipment items like runes, or the zones themselves may be closer to waypoints so they can be cleared faster. For example, both the cow level and Arcane Sanctuary are quite worthwhile despite being level 81 and level 79.


The following chart lists all level 85 zones with the amount of monster types in those zones that have immunities. Some monster types have multiple immunities and contribute toward the amounts in multiple columns. Unique monsters may still have other immunities since they have random bonuses. For example, "2 + 1" means there are 2 normal monster types that spawn with immunities and 1 super unique pack that spawns with immunities.

These immunities haven't changed in PD2 so the Amazon Basin wiki has more comprehensive color-coded resistance/immunity charts for each zone.

info.title: Corrupted Zones
info.html:
• If your character has killed Baal in Hell Difficulty, games made in Hell Difficulty will have Zone(s) "corrupted".
  • Corrupted Zone(s) will gain the following:
    • Monster Level raised to Level 85
    • Increased drop rate of Worldstone Shards and Tier 1 Maps
    • Monster Density increased in most zones (Higher density zones such as Cow Level unchanged)
  • The Zone(s) that are corrupted are chosen somewhat randomly, changing every 15 minutes.
    • To see the current and upcoming Corrupted Zone schedule, see https://pd2.tools/tools/corrupted-zone-tracker and https://exiledagain.github.io/past-dinosaurs/
    • The corrupted Zone(s) are chosen globally and are the same for everyone, on the same schedule.
    • Unlike in Diablo 2: Resurrected, the corrupted Zone(s) do not automatically change; you must quit your game and make a new one for the next Zone to be corrupted.
  • To see all the possible Zone corruptions, see below; Zones listed together corrupt together.

bosses.name: Uber Tristram Prime Evils
bosses.html:
When the final prime evil is defeated, they drop a Hellfire Torch and a Black Soulstone.
  • Uber Tristram is now accessed with Pandemonium Talisman
  • All pre-buffs are removed when characters enter Uber Tristram
  • Players can no longer freely re-enter Uber Tristram while enemies remain within - when first entering the area, three single-use silver portals are created in town and the area may only be re-entered by using them (players get their original attempt plus three extra attempts)
  • Uber Mephisto uses level 20 Conviction (-50% resistances, was -125%)
  • Uber Baal now casts his own version of Lower Resist (-75% resistances, lasts about 25 seconds)
  • Uber Mephisto, Diablo, and Baal now have 10% more health and 25% less defense
  • These ubers no longer drop Standard of Heroes
Uber Diablo is sometimes referred to as "Pandemonium Diablo" with "Uber Diablo" being reserved for Diablo-Clone, but that nomenclature is avoided here.

  • When defeated, a Standard of Heroes will drop. If more than one ancient was fought, each additional ancient beyond the first adds a chance for another to drop.

bosses.name: Diablo-Clone
bosses.html: Diablo-Clone is an endgame boss accessed with a Vision of Terror. Defeating him awards an Annihilus.

bosses.name: Encounter overview
bosses.html:
Entry Use a Vision of Terror at the Blood Fountain in Harrogath.
Difficulty Tier 0, Tier 1 or Tier 2 (change the tier by cubing the Vision of Terror with itself)
Main hazards Cold novas, Meteors, Bone Spirits which create dangerous patches of burning ground on collision, burning ground and skeleton waves
Entry effects Pre-buffs are removed and your mercenary is killed upon entering. Prepare to recast your buffs inside.
Re-entry Tier 0 provides three portals in town. If you die, you will respawn in town as normal and you can enter the arena again, consuming one of the portals. Entering a Tier 0 portal grants temporary invulnerability while you get your body. Re-entry is not possible in Tier 1 and 2
Exit You cannot exit the arena except by killing Diablo-Clone, saving and exiting, or dying.
Guaranteed reward Annihilus

Damage range: Diablo-Clone becomes immune to damage when no player is within approximately 10 yards of him. When in this state the Salvation aura graphic appears at his feet. Ranged characters must remain close enough to damage him.

bosses.name: Monster statistics
bosses.html:
The following are the base Hell-difficulty values in the Season 13 monster data, before additional encounter and tier modifiers.

  • Poison resistance reduces poison damage per frame; PLR (poison length reduction) affects its duration.
  • Curse reduction: 95% leaves 5% of the original duration; the skeletons cannot be cursed.
  • Drain effectiveness scales ordinary life and mana steal, separately from difficulty penalties.
  • Diablo-Clone cannot be chilled.
  • Static Field does not damage Diablo-Clone or skeletons.
  • Diablo-Clone is immune during the skeleton-wave and cold-nova events.

bosses.name: Fight progression
bosses.html:
The fight consists of fighting Diablo-Clone alone, three skeleton waves and three cold-nova sequences, triggered separately by Diablo-Clone's remaining life.

Remaining life Event What happens
Above 85% Opening combat Diablo-Clone uses his regular skills and attacks. Avoid meteors, Bone Spirits and burning ground while damaging him to trigger the first skeleton wave.
Below 85% Skeleton wave 1 Melee skeletons (Bone Warriors) are summoned. Diablo-Clone is immune while the wave remains alive. Defeat the skeletons, then resume damaging him.
Below 75% Cold-nova sequence 1 Diablo-Clone becomes immune, moves toward the centre and releases six cold novas. Meteors and Bone Spirits are not released during the cold-nova sequence.
After sequence 1, until below 60% Combat resumes Diablo-Clone becomes vulnerable and resumes his normal combat attacks. Meteors and Bone Spirits resume; avoid their projectiles and burning ground.
Below 60% Skeleton wave 2 Melee skeletons and Skeleton Archers are summoned. Diablo-Clone is immune while the wave remains alive. Defeat the skeletons, then resume damaging him.
Below 50% Cold-nova sequence 2 Another sequence of six cold novas. Diablo-Clone is immune during the sequence.
After sequence 2, until below 35% Combat resumes Diablo-Clone becomes vulnerable and resumes his normal combat attacks, with meteors, Bone Spirits and burning ground remaining hazards.
Below 35% Skeleton wave 3 Melee skeletons, Skeleton Archers and skeleton mages are summoned. Diablo-Clone is immune while the wave remains alive. Defeat the skeletons, then resume damaging him.
Below 25% Cold-nova sequence 3 The final sequence of six cold novas. Diablo-Clone is immune during the sequence.
After sequence 3 Final combat Diablo-Clone becomes vulnerable and resumes his normal combat attacks. Meteors, Bone Spirits and burning ground remain dangerous. No further scheduled skeleton waves or cold-nova sequences remain.

bosses.name: Diablo-Clone Skills and attacks
bosses.html:
Skill or attack Damage type Description
Firestorm Physical and fire Sends trails of fire along the ground.
Fire nova Fire Releases outward-moving fire projectiles during normal combat.
Lightning hose Physical and lightning Projects a sustained beam toward a target.
Cold melee attack Physical and cold A close-range attack against his target.
Cold nova Cold An arena-wide nova which deal deadly cold damage.

The transition cold novas are separate from his normal fire nova. Despite their internal skill name, UberDiabSuperFire, the transition novas deal cold damage.

bosses.name: Cold novas and pillar positioning
bosses.html:
The transition novas deal cold damage.

  • Diablo-Clone will gain the Salvation aura visual and accompanying sound, and move toward the centre before casting. This is your cue to seek cover. If blocked, he will teleport to the center.
  • Each sequence contains six novas. Successive novas become more dangerous.
  • The novas consist of outward-moving projectiles that pillars (or bodies) can intercept.
  • Cold resistance helps against cold damage, but hiding behind a pillar is the intended way to avoid these projectiles.

bosses.name: Rewards
bosses.html: Defeating Diablo-Clone guarantees an Annihilus. Tier 1 and Tier 2 also have a 1 in 200 chance to drop one of five exclusive unique items. The exclusive items are Overlord's Helm, Dark Abyss, Itherael's Path, Hadriel's Hand and Aidan's Scar.

bosses.name: Rathma and Mendeln
bosses.html: Rathma and Mendeln are endgame bosses accessed with a Voidstone. The encounter includes three clearing stages and three boss fights. Defeating the final pair awards a Tainted Worldstone Shard. "Rathma" can refer to the actual boss, but is a colloquial term for this fight as a whole.

bosses.name: Encounter overview
bosses.html:
Entry Use a Voidstone at the Blood Fountain in Harrogath.
Difficulty Tier 0, Tier 1 or Tier 2 (change the tier by cubing the Voidstone with itself).
Main hazards Poison novas, cold waves, Ancient Spires, Lower Resist, bone spells, damaging ground trails, Conjured Souls and Void Knights.
Entry effects Pre-buffs are removed and your mercenary is killed upon entering. Prepare to recast your buffs inside.
Re-entry Tier 0 provides three single-use portals in town. If you die, you can return through an unused portal. Entering grants temporary invulnerability while you recover your body. Re-entry is not possible in Tier 1 and Tier 2.
Exit You cannot freely leave while enemies remain. Clear each stage to progress through the encounter; otherwise, save and exit or die.
Guaranteed reward Tainted Worldstone Shard after defeating the final Rathma and Mendeln pair.

Final pair: Rathma and Mendeln share life. Damage dealt to either boss reduces their shared life pool; you do not need to defeat two independent life bars.

bosses.name: Monster statistics
bosses.html:
The following are the base Hell-difficulty values in the Season 13 monster data, before additional encounter and tier modifiers. Resistances, PLR, curse reduction, drain and block are percentages.

  • Poison resistance reduces poison damage per frame; PLR affects its duration.
  • Drain effectiveness scales ordinary life and mana steal, separately from difficulty penalties.
  • Mendeln casts Lower Resist in both his solo fight and the final fight. Void Knights can also cast curses, notably Amplify Damage and Lower Resist.

bosses.name: Fight progression
bosses.html:
Unlike the Diablo-Clone and Lucion fights, the Rathma/Mendeln fight consists of three clearing stages alternating with three boss fights. Each of these boss fights have slightly different, but overlapping mechanics. Clear each stage and use its progression portal to reach the next part of the encounter.

Fight Overview

Stage Event What happens
1 Ruins of the Necropolis Travel through this area to get to the portal at the end. You will encounter a range of monsters, such as Burning Souls, Stygian Dolls and Zombies who will drop many needed potions. These mobs also have a chance at non-item drops, such as Trang-oul's Jawbone. It is worth noting that this first stage drops far less potions than the others.
2 Mendeln alone Mendeln uses his regular skills and attacks. Blood-golem events alternate with poison-cloud and long-duration poison-nova events. Ancient Spires add cold-projectile hazards.
3 Decaying Swamplands Travel through this area to get to the portal at the end. You will encounter a range of monsters, such as Burning Souls, Stygian Dolls and Zombies who will drop many needed potions.
4 Rathma alone Rathma uses his regular skills and attacks. At health thresholds he summons Void Knights and becomes immune until they are killed.
5 Decayed Highlands Travel through this area to find the portal in one of three possible spawn places. Here the monsters are Void Knights, Hydras and Frogs.
6 Rathma and Mendeln together Both bosses attack simultaneously and share life. Rathma summons Void Knights; both bosses are immune while the knights remain alive. Mendeln retains his poison-event sequence and Lower Resist, but does not summon the healing blood golems.

Mendeln — solo fight

Mendeln's solo fight alternates between regular combat, four healing waves and three poison sequences. The transitions are triggered by his remaining life.

Remaining life Event What happens
Above 90% Opening combat Mendeln uses his regular skills and attacks, including poison attacks, cold waves and Lower Resist.
Below 90% Healing wave 1 Mendeln becomes immune, teleports to the centre and summons four Sanguine Bearers. Kill them before they reach him to prevent them from healing him.
After wave 1, until below 80% Combat resumes Mendeln becomes vulnerable once the healing wave is resolved and resumes his regular attacks.
Below 80% Poison sequence 1 Mendeln becomes immune and teleports to the centre. He performs a scripted sequence of poison vines, lower resist and poison clouds on the edge of the arena (a delayed portion of the poison vines cast), and after some time a poison nova that has a deadly length. After he casts lower res he will do six regular attacks before casting the poison nova. He remains immune for the beginning of this sequence, and after sometime becomes vulnerable again.
After sequence 1, until below 70% Combat resumes Mendeln becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks. Poison already applied during the sequence can remain active.
Below 70% Healing wave 2 Four more Sanguine Bearers are summoned.
After wave 2, until below 60% Combat resumes Mendeln becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks.
Below 60% Poison sequence 2 Another scripted cold-and-poison sequence.
After sequence 2, until below 50% Combat resumes Mendeln becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks.
Below 50% Healing wave 3 Four more Sanguine Bearers are summoned.
After wave 3, until below 40% Combat resumes Mendeln becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks.
Below 40% Poison sequence 3 The third scripted cold-and-poison sequence.
After sequence 3, until below 30% Combat resumes Mendeln becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks.
Below 30% Healing wave 4 The final four Sanguine Bearers are summoned.
After wave 4, until below 15% Final combat Mendeln becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks. No further healing waves are scheduled.
Below 15% Retreat Mendeln becomes immune and leaves the solo fight. A progression portal opens for the next stage.

Rathma — solo fight

Rathma begins summoning Conjured Souls below 80% life. Three Void Knight waves interrupt the fight at separate life thresholds.

Remaining life Event What happens
Above 80% Opening combat Rathma uses his regular skills and attacks, including Bone Spears, Teeth and Bone Novas.
Below 80% Conjured Souls begin Rathma summons a Conjured Soul. Further Conjured Souls can be summoned during combat, adding fire hazards to his bone spells and ground trails.
Until below 70% Combat continues Rathma continues his regular attacks while Conjured Souls add fire hazards.
Below 70% Void Knight wave 1 Four Void Knights are summoned: one cold, two fire and one poison. Rathma becomes immune while the knights remain alive.
After wave 1, until below 50% Combat resumes Rathma becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks.
Below 50% Void Knight wave 2 Five Void Knights are summoned: one cold, one fire, two poison and one physical.
After wave 2, until below 30% Combat resumes Rathma becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks.
Below 30% Void Knight wave 3 Six Void Knights are summoned: two cold, two fire, one poison and one physical.
After wave 3, until below 15% Final combat Rathma becomes vulnerable and resumes his regular attacks. No further Void Knight waves are scheduled.
Below 15% Retreat Rathma becomes immune and leaves the solo fight. A progression portal opens for the next stage.

Rathma and Mendeln — final clone fight

Both bosses attack simultaneously and share life. Mendeln's poison sequences alternate with Rathma's Void Knight waves. Mendeln does not summon Sanguine Bearers in this fight, and there are no Ancient Spires.

Remaining life Event What happens
Above 80% Opening combat Both bosses use their regular skills and attacks.
Below 80% Poison sequence 1
Conjured Souls begin 		Mendeln teleports to the centre, becomes immune briefly and performs his poison sequence. Rathma is vulnerable throughout and begins summoning Conjured Souls throughout the remainder of the fight, while attacking as normal.
After sequence 1, until below 70% Combat resumes Mendeln is again able to move around and both bosses continue attacking.
Below 70% Void Knight wave 1 Four Void Knights are summoned: one cold, two fire and one poison. Both bosses are immune while the knights remain alive.
After wave 1, until below 60% Combat resumes Both bosses become vulnerable and resume combat.
Below 60% Poison sequence 2 Mendeln teleports to the centre, becomes immune briefly and performs his poison sequence. Rathma remains a separate source of attacks.
After sequence 2, until below 50% Combat resumes Mendeln is again able to move around and both bosses continue attacking.
Below 50% Void Knight wave 2 Five Void Knights are summoned: one cold, one fire, two poison and one physical.
After wave 2, until below 40% Combat resumes Both bosses become vulnerable and resume combat.
Below 40% Poison sequence 3 Mendeln teleports to the centre, becomes immune briefly and performs his poison sequence. Rathma remains a separate source of attacks.
After sequence 3, until below 30% Combat resumes Mendeln is again able to move around and both bosses continue attacking.
Below 30% Void Knight wave 3 Six Void Knights are summoned: two cold, two fire, one poison and one physical. Both bosses are immune while the knights remain alive.
After wave 3, until below 20% Combat resumes Both bosses become vulnerable and resume combat. No further Void Knight waves are scheduled.
Below 20% Poison sequence 4 Mendeln's final poison sequence.
After sequence 4 Final combat Mendeln becomes vulnerable and both bosses continue attacking until their shared life is depleted. No further scheduled Void Knight waves or poison-sequence transitions remain.
  • The life-sharing mechanic means your damage is halved, but applied to both bosses regardless of who you hit. As of S13 your poison length is also halved, which means poison builds will deal less damage than non-poison builds.

bosses.name: Rewards
bosses.html:
Defeating the final pair guarantees a Tainted Worldstone Shard, used to corrupt an Annihilus.

Tier 1–2: 1 in 200 chance for one of The Third Eye, Band of Skulls or Cage of the Unsullied. Each item has an equal chance within this roll.

Separate utility-item roll: an equal chance to select one of Skeleton Key, Horadric Almanac or Horadric Navigator. The chance for any one of these items is 1 in 50 in Tier 0, 1 in 44 in Tier 1, and 1 in 38 in Tier 2.

The unique-item and utility-item rolls are separate; both can succeed on the same kill.

bosses.name: Lucion
bosses.html: Lucion is an endgame boss accessed with a Shadow of Hatred. Defeating him grants access to the Temple of the Triune, where an amulet can receive a desecration attempt.

bosses.name: Encounter overview
bosses.html:
Entry Use a Shadow of Hatred at the Blood Fountain in Harrogath.
Difficulty Tier 0, Tier 1 or Tier 2 (change the tier by cubing the Shadow of Hatred with itself).
Main hazards Lightning novas, lightning ground effects, physical attacks, stuns and minion-spawning portals.
Entry effects Pre-buffs are removed and your mercenary is killed upon entering. Prepare to recast your buffs inside.
Re-entry Tier 0 provides three single-use portals in town. If you die, you can return through an unused portal. Entering grants temporary invulnerability while you recover your body. Re-entry is not possible in Tier 1 and Tier 2.
Exit You cannot freely leave while the encounter is active. Defeat Lucion, save and exit, or die.
Guaranteed reward Access to the Temple of the Triune for an amulet desecration attempt. A successful desecration is not guaranteed.

bosses.name: Monster statistics
bosses.html:
The following are the base Hell-difficulty values in the Season 13 monster data, before additional encounter and tier modifiers. Resistances, PLR, curse reduction, drain and block are percentages.

  • Poison resistance reduces poison damage per frame; PLR affects its duration.
  • Lucion cannot be frozen.
  • Drain effectiveness scales ordinary life and mana steal, separately from difficulty penalties.

bosses.name: Fight progression
bosses.html:
Lucion's regular combat is interrupted by portal and lightning-nova sequences. The encounter can continue cycling through these events if he remains alive.

Event What happens
Opening combat Lucion uses his regular skills and attacks, including physical attacks and repositioning abilities.
Portal sequence Lucion disappears and Veiled Portals spawn minions. Destroy the portals to reduce further spawns and clear dangerous enemies.
Combat resumes Lucion returns. Remaining minions can continue attacking while you fight him.
Lightning-nova sequence Lucion moves to the centre and releases lightning waves. Watch their pattern and move through the gaps.
Later combat Portal and nova events remain part of the fight. Continue controlling minions and avoiding ground hazards until Lucion is defeated.
Lucion defeated Progress to the Temple of the Triune for the amulet desecration attempt and golden chests.
  • Unlike Diablo-Clone and Rathma/Mendeln, Lucion is never visible and invulnerable. The only time he cannot take damage is when he disappears.

bosses.name: Lightning novas and positioning
bosses.html:
• Watch Lucion's movement toward the centre and the start of the nova animation.
  • The nova uses slow, weaker wave to allow you time to seek the right position and the fast lightning waves can be deadly.

bosses.html:
Defeating Lucion grants access to the Temple of the Triune. An amulet desecration can add a second corruption modifier, but success is not guaranteed.

info.title: Prime Evils
info.html:
Monsters with the Prime Evil tag all come with additional buffs. Prime Evil monsters include:

  • All act bosses, classic bosses and classic ubers
  • All map bosses
  • All dungeon monsters and bosses
  • All new ubers and their minions


The additional buffs that they gain are:

  • 200% damage to minions and mercenaries
  • Immune to slow effects (cold damage, Decrepify, Holy Freeze, Slows Target by X%, etc.)
  • Immune to Dim Vision, Terror, Confuse, and Attract
  • Immune to Sanctuary's physical resistance removal

info.title: Special Monsters
info.html: Mephisto, Diablo, and Baal now have a chance to drop Prime Evil Soul in Hell difficulty.

Three additional enemies drop Uber Keys: Blood Raven, Bloodwitch, and Izual

info.title: Ubers
info.html:
All ubers regenerate life like most monsters, but their high life means they regenerate substantially more per second than most. Monsters do not regenerate life while being damaged, so continuous damage such as Poison Damage or Open Wounds will halt their regeneration entirely. Prevent Monster Heal does not affect ubers. Note that ubers' immunities are not shown beneath their name like they are for other monsters.

Ubers within Uber Tristram no longer regenerate health

Drain: It's the effectiveness as percentage applied to life and mana returned by "% Life Stolen per Hit" and "% Mana Stolen per Hit".

Crit Chance: It's the ability of the monster to deal double damage.
